label: Contact Dynamics
notes: Welcome to Lecture 11, printed pages 61 to 64. Last time we built the contact structure as a maximally non-integrable hyperplane field. Today we turn that static geometry into motion: every contact form secretes a canonical vector field, the Reeb field, whose flow drives all of contact dynamics and connects to the Weinstein conjecture.

label: The Reeb Vector Field
notes: The Reeb field is pinned down by two linear conditions on the tangent space at each point. The interior product with d-alpha kills it, which forces it into the kernel of d-alpha, and the normalization alpha of R equals one fixes its length transverse to the contact planes. Together these give a unique R.

label: Why R Is Well Defined
notes: Stress why the two equations have exactly one solution. On a contact manifold d-alpha restricted to the contact hyperplane is nondegenerate, so its kernel in the full tangent space is one dimensional and transverse to that hyperplane. The normalization then selects a single vector from that line, giving a globally defined smooth field.

label: The Reeb Flow Preserves Alpha
notes: Run Cartan's magic formula on the Lie derivative of alpha along R. The exterior derivative term and the interior product term both vanish by the defining equations, so the Lie derivative is zero. The flow therefore preserves both alpha and d-alpha, making it a one parameter group of strict contactomorphisms.

label: Transverse to the Contact Planes
notes: This is the key picture: at every point R pokes straight through the contact plane while d-alpha is nondegenerate inside the plane. Have students trace one flow line climbing through a stack of tilted planes. Emphasise that R is never tangent to the distribution, unlike Legendrian directions coming later.

label: Model Reeb Flows
notes: Two anchoring examples. In standard contact Euclidean space the Reeb field is just vertical translation, so orbits are open lines climbing in z. On the odd sphere the same equations yield the Hopf field, rotating every complex coordinate at equal speed, so every orbit is a closed Hopf circle. Same recipe, very different dynamics.

label: Contact Vector Fields and Hamiltonians
notes: Generalise from R to all contact vector fields, whose flows preserve the contact distribution up to scale. The crucial fact is that these are in bijection with smooth functions, the contact Hamiltonians, via H equals alpha of X. So the contactomorphism group is parametrised by functions, exactly as symplectic flows are generated by Hamiltonians.

label: Legendrian Submanifolds
notes: Legendrians are the contact analogue of Lagrangians: n dimensional submanifolds everywhere tangent to the contact hyperplane field, which is the maximal possible isotropic dimension. Contrast them sharply with Reeb orbits, which are always transverse. The Legendrian condition pulls alpha back to zero, and these submanifolds carry their own rich knot theory.

label: Symplectization
notes: Symplectization is the bridge back to symplectic geometry. Adjoin a real coordinate tau and form omega as the exterior derivative of e-to-the-tau times alpha. A short computation shows omega is nondegenerate, so the contact manifold becomes a hypersurface in a symplectic cone and Reeb dynamics is the restricted Hamiltonian flow on that level.

label: Reeb Orbits and Weinstein
notes: Periodic Reeb orbits are the central objects. Seifert asked about closed orbits for general vector fields and there are counterexamples, but the Weinstein conjecture concerns the rigid Reeb fields of contact forms on closed manifolds and predicts a closed orbit always exists. Mention Hofer's and Viterbo's landmark cases and Taubes's three dimensional theorem.

label: Geodesic Flow as a Reeb Flow
notes: The flagship example: on the unit cotangent bundle the canonical one form restricts to a contact form whose Reeb flow is exactly the geodesic flow of the base metric. Closed Reeb orbits become closed geodesics, so Weinstein type existence results recover and generalise classical theorems on the existence of periodic geodesics.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Recap the chain: contact form gives a Reeb field, whose flow preserves alpha and lives transverse to the planes; contact vector fields correspond to Hamiltonian functions; Legendrians are the tangent extremes; symplectization links everything to symplectic geometry; and Reeb orbits feed the Weinstein conjecture. Next we move toward almost complex structures and compatible triples.
